=== page 4 ===
OUR MARKET DEBUT
Our listing at BSE Limited and the NSE Limited marked a watershed moment in 
Pine Labs’ evolution as an institution. The strong response to our public offering, 
reflected in its oversubscription, highlighted investor confidence in the resilience of 
our business model, the scale of our opportunity and our ability to create enduring 
value as a public company.
Our ~H 3900 Crores IPO, structured as a fresh issue 
of H2,080 Crores alongside an Offer for Sale of 
H1,819.9 Crores expanded our shareholder base 
and also drew participation from some of most 
respected institutional investors, demonstrating 
strong conviction in our growth story. The breadth 
of participation spanning domestic mutual funds, 
foreign institutional investors, long-only funds, 
high-net-worth individuals and retail investors reflected the expanded recognition of Pine Labs 
as a category-defining commerce infrastructure 
platform. The listing was a collective endorsement of 
our technology-driven business and our ambition to 
scale across India and beyond. The proceeds from 
the fresh issue would be channelled into deepening 
our technology infrastructure and accelerating 
international expansion, laying a firm foundation for 
the next phase of purposeful, sustainable growth.
=== page 5 ===
A LETTER FROM OUR CEO
B. Amrish Rau  
Chairman, Managing Director,
and Chief Executive Officer, 
Pine LabsDear Members, 
 
Winning transactions sounds simple. But 
it is the hardest thing to do consistently, at 
scale, across merchants, markets, banks, 
and rails that are constantly changing 
underneath. It is also the belief that has 
shaped every decision we have made at Pine 
Labs, and every layer of infrastructure we 
have built beneath it.
Every transaction is a vote of confidence, 
from a consumer, a merchant, a brand, 
or a financial institution. Our journey 
has therefore been about continuously 
increasing the number of transactions we 
win, while expanding the value we create 
around each one.
FY 2025-26 was another important step in that journey — and our first full year of 
profitability. Our platforms processed $194 Billion of GTV, up 50% year on year, across 740 
Crores+ transactions. Revenue from operations grew 19% to ₹2,711 Crores, Adjusted EBITDA 
grew 57% to ₹559 Crores with margins expanding to 21%, and we delivered PAT of ₹113 Crores  
compared with a loss of ₹145 Crores in FY 2024-25. Operating cash flow increased eight-
fold to ₹395 Crores. That swing to profitability demonstrates the operating leverage inherent 
in the platform we have built: as our businesses scale, technology and infrastructure 
investments support significantly greater volumes without a proportionate increase in our 
cost base. 
We now serve more than 11 Lakhs Merchants, with over 20 Lakhs+ digital checkout points  
across our markets. But for us, these numbers are not the destination. They are the foundation 
on which we are building the next phase of Pine Labs.
This is also our first annual report since our IPO, and I want to use it to explain the architecture 
of what we are building, and why it matters more now than at any point since we started.
 
FROM PAYMENTS TO FULL STACK COMMERCE
You may still think of us as an offline payments company. We’ll take that—that’s where you 
first saw us win. But that’s not the whole picture: we don’t see online or offline. We only see the 
transaction. And we’ve built to win it, wherever it happens.
Annual Report 2025-26  |  2
Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements
=== page 6 ===
We started with payments acceptance. We then built capabilities around the transaction: 
affordability, EMI, offers, loyalty, issuing, prepaid, online payments, transaction processing, 
and fintech infrastructure. Today, our offerings are increasingly full stack.
Banks want to keep their merchant relationships. Merchants want faster, simpler payment 
systems. Brands want to hold the money that keeps a customer coming back. Pine Labs sits 
inside all three relationships at once, which is why the stack matters more than any single 
layer in it.
Banks want to keep their 
merchant relationships. 
Merchants want faster, 
simpler payment 
systems. Brands want 
to hold the money 
that keeps a customer 
coming back. Pine 
Labs sits inside all three 
relationships at once, 
which is why the stack 
matters more than any 
single layer in it.We view that stack as a four-layered 
architecture: payment rails at the foundation, 
processing infrastructure above it, orchestration 
above that, and financial platforms at the top. 
Simple enough to remember, complex enough 
to have taken years to build.
The moat is in the layers underneath: regulatory 
licences, scheme certifications, years of becoming 
the system of record that banks trust with 
settlement. That is not a feature you ship. It is 
a position you earn, and it compounds. Banks 
and merchants are running on our infrastructure, 
making switching a migration of the system 
of record itself. The more transactions we win, 
the more relationships and products we can 
offer. And the more products we offer, the more 
valuable our platform becomes.

TAKING PINE LABS GLOBAL
India has been an extraordinary laboratory for digital commerce. The scale, diversity, and 
complexity of the Indian market forced us to build products that are resilient, configurable, 
and capable of operating at enormous transaction volumes. Many emerging markets are now 
at a similar inflection point.
Across these markets, three forces are converging. Consumers expect the digital commerce 
they’ve seen in India—now. Banks sense they’re falling behind their own customers’ 
expectations. In Indonesia, our banking partners echo what we heard in India a decade 
ago: urgency to modernise before fintechs redefine the relationship. And regulators across 
Southeast Asia, Africa, and Latin America are studying India’s model of open, interoperable 
infrastructure as a blueprint to adapt.
Our international business has grown at a 44% CAGR over the last three years and now 
contributes approximately 15% of our revenues, up from 9% three years ago, across 22 
countries. Our ambition is not to export an Indian product unchanged. It is to export 
the Pine Labs platform, and build a global fintech company that localises that platform 
market by market.
 
BUILDING FOR THE NEXT NOW
Commerce is entering a new era: agentic 
commerce. For thirty years, digital commerce meant 
a human on a screen. That model is giving way to 
AI agents that discover, negotiate, and transact 
autonomously. The transaction surface is shifting 
from apps to prompts, and payments infrastructure 
must move with it.
We have made significant progress here. Agentic 
commerce doesn’t start from zero—it needs rails 
that already work at scale. Pine Labs is today one 
of the largest players in online and bill payments 
in India, processing at a scale that gives us a 
vantage point few others have into how commerce 
is actually changing. This is not a peripheral bet for 
us — it is where we are directing significant focus and 
investment, because we believe the infrastructure 
that wins agentic commerce will be built by those 
who already understand payments at scale, not by 
those retrofitting it in.
We built India’s first autonomous agentic 
payments protocol on top of UPI—a compliance-first 
architecture where buyer and seller agents discover, 
Annual Report 2025-26  |  4
Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements

=== page 8 ===
negotiate, and complete transactions autonomously within established regulatory guardrails. 
We are calling it P3P. The question is not whether agentic commerce arrives. It is whether the 
payments infrastructure underneath it is ready. Most of it is not. P3P is Pine Labs’ answer to 
that gap.
This same pattern—infrastructure built for yesterday struggling with today’s reality—shows 
up in credit. Consumer behaviour has shifted: today, close to 80% of a bank statement is UPI 
narrations. Legacy parsers cannot read them. Pine Labs can, because years of processing 
payments has given us the pattern intelligence to interpret what those narrations say 
about a borrower’s real financial behaviour. That capability is now a product: SignalIQ, 
comprehensive bank statement analyser that can read 100% of bank statements.
AI is not a layer we are adding on top of the stack. It is embedded at every level: smart 
routing, anomaly detection, Edge AI auto-healing across 2 Million touchpoints, 1.5 Million lines 
of code updated monthly through AI-assisted tooling, and half of customer emails resolved in 
under a minute.
We are deliberate about where we focus: we empower banks, merchants, and brands rather 
than competing with them for consumer ownership. How we expand consumer touchpoints 
remains an active question, but our core moat stays the infrastructure beneath. Our 
investments in AI, data, and agentic payments are not a departure from our strategy—they 
are the next logical extension of it.
 
THE JOURNEY
We started with a simple ambition: win transactions. We have built a full-stack commerce 
platform around those transactions. We are taking that platform global. And we are now 
preparing it for a world in which commerce itself is increasingly intelligent, autonomous, and 
agent-driven.
What we have built underneath the surface—a commerce operating system running quietly 
beneath billions of transactions a year—is what I am proudest of. Most people who benefit 
from it will never know it exists. That is exactly how infrastructure is supposed to work.
Thank you for building this with us, and for trusting us with the part of your business that has 
to work every time.  
Yours sincerely,  
B. Amrish Rau 
Chairman, Managing Director,  
and Chief Executive Officer,   
Pine Labs

ABOUT US
Powering an integrated commerce ecosystem 
For over two decades, we have operated at the intersection of commerce and 
technology, continuously evolving alongside the merchants, financial institutions, 
consumer brands and enterprises we serve. 
Today, we are one of India’s 
leading fintech and commerce 
infrastructure platform built to win 
transactions wherever commerce 
happens — in-store, online and 
increasingly through emerging 
digital and agentic experiences. 
From our origins in payment 
acceptance, we have expanded 
our capabilities across transaction 
processing, affordability, issuing, 
prepaid, online payments, data 
and financial infrastructure.
SuccessOur full-stack offering enables 
merchants, brands and financial 
institutions to access multiple 
capabilities under an integrated 
platform and grow their businesses. 
Today, over 20 Lakhs+ DCP’s, 11 
Lakhs+ Merchants, 750+ consumer 
brands and enterprises, and 200+ 
financial institutions operate on 
Our infrastructure, generating 
$194Bn+ annual GTV across 740 
Crores+ transactions. This creates 
a powerful three-sided network 
in which every new participant 
enhances the value of the platform 
for existing participants. 
Our long-term strategy is 
anchored in three dimensions 
that together define our North 
Star: a multiproduct platform 
spanning the full commerce stack, 
a multi-segment reach from 
large enterprises to SMEs, and a 
multimarket footprint that enables 
us to export India’s battle-tested 
fintech infrastructure to emerging 
and developed markets.
At the heart of our platform are 
four core capabilities: simplifying 
checkout across commerce 
surfaces; enabling brands and 
financial institutions to issue, accept, 
store and move currency at scale; 
providing leading affordability 
marketplaces; and converting 
transaction data into actionable 
merchant intelligence through our 
software platform.
We have built a deeply integrated, 
highly embedded and sticky 
distribution infrastructure, strengthened by bespoke, flow-
based payment solutions on a 
single platform. This foundation 
has enabled expansion into fast-
growing Brand and Consumer 
value pools through affordability 
and prepaid issuing, with Business 
Services, Data and AI emerging as 
the next frontier for creating new 
opportunities across commerce.
Our technology processes billions 
of transactions annually across a 
diverse retail, digital and institutional 
commerce landscape. As we expand 
our presence across international 
markets, we remain focused on 
building solutions designed for the 
scale, complexity and diversity of 
emerging economies. Our ambition 
is to build future-ready commerce 
infrastructure for the Global 
South, empowering businesses to 
participate in the digital economy 
with greater efficiency, accessibility 
and resilience.

OUR PERFORMANCE IN NUMBERS
Financial performance
FY 2025-26 marked a defining year in our evolution, demonstrating the strength of 
our platform-led growth model. Over the last three years, we scaled our platform 
GTV at a CAGR of 57%, During FY 2025-26, we processed more than 2 Crores 
transactions daily and expanded our DCP’s base to 20.3 Lakhs devices, translating 
into sustained revenue growth. 
Over last three years our revenue expanded at CAGR 
of 19% while expanding International revenues at the 
CAGR of 44% during the same period.  The composition 
of our revenues is steadily shifting towards higher-
value, higher-margin businesses, reflecting the 
increasing monetisation of our platform and creating 
a stronger foundation for sustainable profitability. 
This momentum is driving significant expansion in our 
profitability, with Adjusted EBITDA margin improving from 9% in FY 2023-24 to 21% in FY 2025-26. We also 
reported a Profit After Tax (PAT) of H113 Crores in  
FY 2025-26, reversing from loss of H145 Crores in  
FY 2024-25, while improving our operating cash flow 
by over 8x  to H395 Crores during the same period. 
These milestones reflect the successful conversion of 
scale into profitability and cash generation, creating a 
stronger foundation for long-term growth.

THE ENGINES BEHIND LONG-TERM VALUE CREATION
We are building a commerce OS that enables merchants, consumer brands, financial 
institutions and consumers to participate in the digital economy. Our platform brings 
together a connected ecosystem that supports the entire transaction lifecycle.
Built on a scalable technology foundation, our solutions simplify commerce by integrating payments, 
engagement, data and affordability solutions into a unified platform. Each capability strengthens the others, 
creating powerful network effects that enhance customer experiences, unlock new revenue opportunities and 
drive long-term growth.
Together, these interconnected growth engines position us at the centre of the rapidly evolving commerce 
ecosystem.

2. Online payment 
Pine Labs Online is our cloud-based 
payments platform for online-first 
and omnichannel merchants. Our 
payment gateway lets businesses 
collect payments across form 
factors like cards, net banking, 
UPI and wallets; payment links let 
merchants collect money through 
a simple link over email or SMS, with 
no website or app needed; and 
payouts enable instant transfers 
for refunds, vendor payments and 
salaries. Easy to integrate and built 
for high transaction success rates, 
the platform comes with affordability 
solutions, recurring payments 
and business analytics built in. 
It is today one of India's fastest-
growing payments and bill payment infrastructure platforms, trusted by 
the country's leading e-commerce 
and quick commerce companies — 
a measure of its enterprise-grade 
reliability and scale.
Product velocity remains a 
hallmark of the business, with

B. FLOW, AFFORDABILITY & TRANSACTION PROCESSING 
1. Affordability
Our affordability solutions make purchases more accessible for consumers and drive higher sales for merchants. At 
checkout — whether in-store, online or through a payment link — consumers can convert their purchase into easy 
monthly instalments, claim instant cashback/discounts or unlock sponsored offers, all presented in real time through 
our digital multi-lender platform. The experience is simple and paperless: consumers can identify themselves with 
a card, mobile number or PAN, compare offers through an intuitive EMI calculator, and complete their purchase in 
moments. Importantly, we do not take on any consumer credit risk — we are the technology and orchestration layer 
that makes the transaction seamless.

What makes the platform powerful is the ecosystem we bring together. Merchants use our affordability 
solutions to convert more customers, drive premiumisation and increase ticket sizes; consumer brands 
run their own sponsored promotions — zero-cost/low cost financing, instant discounts and cashbacks — 
to drive demand for their products; and financial institutions disperse new credit including to consumers

eligibility checks, authentication, fraud mitigation and the smooth transfer of subvention costs from 
brands to lenders. The breadth of this network is itself the value: the more lenders and brands on the 
platform, the richer the offers a merchant can present, and the better the experience for the consumer.

C. FINTECH INFRASTRUCTURE  
Our API-led fintech infrastructure platform is positioned at the operating layer of India’s digital public infrastructure — the 
layer that sits on top of the rails the country has built and given away. We run on two engines that reinforce each other: 
real-time payments and credit insights. Payments generate rich, consented transaction data; that data sharpens credit 
decisions; and better credit deepens engagement back on the payment rails — a compounding flywheel that few in the 
ecosystem can replicate. We provide these building blocks through three pillars:
Real-time payments: As a 
technology service provider for UPI 
and Bharat Connect, we help banks 
and fintechs run the payment rail 
itself — accepting payments in 
their own apps through QR codes, 
links and recurring mandates, 
and embedding bill payments 
so consumers can settle utility, 
loan and insurance bills in a 
few clicks, with onboarding, 
reconciliation and settlement built 
in. Bill payments are a powerful 
wedge for our partners to deepen 
everyday customer engagement.Identity: Our APIs make 
customer onboarding fully 
digital — Aadhaar-based KYC 
and business verification, PAN 
and bank account checks, 
and digitally signed contracts 
— so institutions can acquire 
individuals and businesses faster, 
without paperwork, while staying 
compliant.Data: With customer consent, 
we help lenders see a borrower’s 
complete financial picture. Our 
Account Aggregator gateway 
brings data from multiple sources 
into one place, and our insights 
engine turns it into a clear read 
of income, obligations and 
repayment capacity — supporting 
better decisions across acquisition, 
underwriting, collections and 
engagement.

Our credit engine is built on a simple 
principle: every loan needs three 
things — knowing who the borrower 
is, knowing how they earn, and 
catching stress early. Identity and 
onboarding answer the first; our 
underwriting capabilities answer 
the second, producing the accurate 
picture of a borrower's fixed-
obligation-to-income position the 
industry has seen by combining 
payment flows with consented 
data, and surfacing a richer, better-
quality approved cohort than a 
bureau score alone can identify. 
The third is answered by SignalIQ, 
our monitoring engine, which 
watches the payment rail rather 
than the repayment record — so signs of financial stress, such as 
shifts in spending patterns or rising 
obligations, show up well before an 
instalment is missed, giving lenders 
lead time to act.
We are bringing the same foresight 
to the evolution of commerce 
itself. As consumers increasingly 
transact through AI assistants 
rather than applications, we are 
building the infrastructure for this 
transition: agentic bill payments, 
enabling an assistant to discover, 
schedule and settle a consumer's 
bills automatically, and agentic 
commerce, enabling it to identify 
the right merchant, compare 
options and complete a purchase securely and with consent on the 
consumer's behalf. India has built 
world-class digital payment rails; 
we are building the intelligent 
operating layer above them — 
positioning us at the centre of how 
India will transact, borrow and pay 
in the decade ahead.

D. ISSUING AND ACQUIRING PLATFORM 
Issuing and Acquiring Platform
Our Issuing and Acquiring 
Platform operates through two 
businesses: Pine Labs Prepaid, a 
global technology platform for 
consumer brands and enterprises 
to create prepaid products that 
help them drive sales and Credit+, 
an API-first issuing, acquiring, and 
processing infrastructure for banks 
and Fintechs to issue credit, debit, 
forex and prepaid instruments to 
their end consumers and to offer 
merchant acquiring services.
Pine Labs Prepaid
Generic money has no memory, 
no rules, and no loyalty. A 
merchant cannot prevent refunds 
from leaking to competitors. An 
e-commerce platform cannot 
guarantee a first-time buyer 
returns. An employer cannot 
govern how an allowance is 
spent. Pine Labs Prepaid solves 
this — embedding intent into every transaction and defining 
who spends, how much, where, 
when, and on what. The platform 
enables brands to acquire new 
consumers, commit future spend, 
influence behaviour, and govern 
usage. Prepaid, in short, helps 
brands acquire, retain, grow, and 
engage with their customers.
The platform supports three 
instrument types. Closed-loop 
instruments anchor spend at a 
single merchant — ideal for gift 
cards, store credits, and refunds. 
Semi-closed loop instruments 
extend redemption across a 
curated merchant network, 
powering multi-brand rewards 
and incentives. Open-loop 
instruments run on interoperable 
networks for the broadest 
consumer reach. All three 
operate across a common stack 
spanning gifting, promotions, 
cashbacks, employee benefits, 
channel incentives, mobility and 
other use cases — live across 
India, Southeast Asia, the UAE, 
and Australia, with early success 
in the United States as well.The platform is built to embed 
into existing merchant workflows, 
not sit alongside them. Open 
APIs connect directly into point-
of-sale, e-commerce, and 
mobile environments. Program 
management lets businesses 
define precise spend rules 
— who, where, when, and on 
what. A real-time processing 
engine authorises and settles 
transactions at scale. Enterprise 
APIs deliver live reporting, audit 
trails, and ERP integrations. 
Compliance is built into the 
platform, with KYC, AML and 
Video KYC embedded into the 
onboarding journey rather than 
added as standalone processes.
Distribution is where the 
platform's moat is amplified. 
Woohoo, Pine Labs' consumer-
facing store, enables instant 
digital gift card purchase and 
delivery — locking in tomorrow's 
spend today. White-labelled 
storefronts give merchants 
their own branded channel 
for consumer and corporate 
distribution. The Rewards 
Catalogue enables structured 
corporate reward programmes. 
Engage Hub consolidates 
gamification, personalisation, 
campaign management, and 
incentive mechanics into one 
platform — eliminating the 
need to stitch together multiple 
vendors.

TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION
The Platform That Powers Digital Payments
Our technology platform is designed as a full-stack, cloud-based, flexible and 
scalable infrastructure that simplifies payments while enabling affordability 
solutions to be  embedded into merchant and consumer journeys. Built on 
a platform-first approach, it treats payments as foundational infrastructure

 — Cloud InfrastructureThe Platform That Powers Issuing
Our issuing technology platform is designed as a full-stack, cloud-based, 
flexible and scalable infrastructure that unifies prepaid issuance, processing 
and program management into a single, API-first environment.
Built on a cloud-native, modular architecture, the platform integrates onboarding, issuance, transaction 
processing, programme rules and reporting into one end-to-end system. This design reduces integration 
complexity while delivering consistent, reliable performance across geographies, currencies and use cases.

RE-WIRING THE ORGANISATION FOR THE AI ERA
Every generation encounters a technology that fundamentally reshapes the 
competitive landscape. Today, that technology is artificial intelligence. For a 
company built over more than two decades powering payments and commerce, 
it is prompting us to re-examine not just how we operate, but how we innovate, 
create value and lead.
AI entered the mainstream only two years ago, yet the pace of change since has been relentless, with 
models, capabilities and expectations evolving almost every month. There is no definitive blueprint for 
what fintech and commerce will look like on the other side of this transformation, and we have chosen not 
to wait for one to emerge. Instead, we are shaping our own path, using AI as the foundation to experiment, 
innovate and redefine the future of commerce alongside the entrepreneurs and businesses we serve. It 
is a natural progression in our journey from payments to commerce infrastructure, now unfolding at an 
unprecedented pace.

Our ambition is to build an

=== page 48 ===
Compensation Philosophy
Our compensation philosophy 
rests on a single conviction: people 
who build enduring value should 
share in it.
We link pay directly to contribution 
and impact - not tenure, not 
hierarchy. Our framework is 
designed to reward those who 
deliver outsized outcomes, who 
strengthen the organisation 
around them and who take 
genuine ownership of Pine Labs’ 
long-term success. We reward 
results, and the behaviours that 
make results repeatable.
As a listed company, equity 
ownership is central to how we 
think about long-term alignment. Ahead of our IPO, we deliberately 
redesigned our equity framework, 
moving away from a single deeply 
discounted ESOP structure towards 
a combination model comprising 
market-value grants, performance-
linked equity and a selective 
deep-discount component. This 
architecture ensures that equity 
ownership at Pine Labs is earned 
through contribution and aligned to 
shareholder value creation and not 
simply awarded through tenure. 
Our Variable Pay Framework 
reinforces the same logic. Payouts 
are linked to business performance 
and individual impact ensuring 
that in strong years, the people 
who drove that performance are meaningfully recognised, and that 
in difficult years, the framework 
maintains credibility rather than 
becoming disconnected from 
commercial reality.
We recognise that compensation 
alone does not retain the people 
who build institutions. But getting 
it wrong, failing to differentiate, 
failing to share value creation, 
failing to signal clearly what Pine 
Labs rewards, is a cost we cannot 
afford. We therefore review our 
reward architecture continuously, 
with the goal of remaining 
competitive in the markets we 
operate in and credible to the 
people we most want to keep.
Innovation Anchored in Customer Problems
We anchor innovation in real customer problems, ensuring that the solutions our teams build are relevant, scalable, 
and capable of delivering meaningful impact rather than innovation for its own sake. To operationalise this, we create 
dedicated platforms such as hackathons and innovation sprints, giving teams structured space to experiment, 
prototype, and pitch bold ideas beyond their day-to-day responsibilities. This approach ensures innovation is not 
confined to a single team or function but distributed across the organisation as a shared discipline. It also creates a 
pipeline of new ideas that can be tested quickly and, where validated, scaled into the core business. This is central to 
how Pine Labs intends to keep bringing new products to market ahead of where the industry is heading.

=== page 49 ===
Employee Engagement
Our approach to employee engagement 
is anchored in a strong philosophy built 
on four key pillars - To Belong, To Be 
Valued, To Be Heard, and To Be Inspired. 
These pillars are not abstract values 
but the organising framework behind 
our annual engagement calendar, 
which includes more than 40 activities 
delivered across both online and offline 
formats. Every activity is thoughtfully 
curated to keep these four pillars at its 
core, ensuring engagement efforts are 
intentional rather than generic. This 
structured approach reflects our belief 
that engagement is a deliberate design 
choice, not something that happens 
incidentally. It is one of the mechanisms 
through which we reinforce our culture 
code in the everyday employee 
experience.
Health and Well-being
Employee health and well-being at Pine Labs is not treated as a peripheral initiative. It is a deliberate investment 
in our people’s ability to perform. Our approach is built around a supportive ecosystem that addresses physical, 
mental, and emotional health as interconnected dimensions of well-being. This reflects our recognition that 
people perform at their best when they are supported as whole individuals, not just as employees executing 
tasks. By embedding well-being into our core people philosophy, we aim to build long-term resilience across 
the organisation rather than offering reactive support. This is particularly important as we scale at pace, where 
sustained performance depends on people being genuinely supported.

Diversity and  Inclusion

measure ourselves not by the talent we attract

and more valuable than it was the year before.

ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP IN MOTION
For a technology-led business, environmental leadership is defined less by the 
footprint of our offices than by the footprint of the commerce we enable. We do 
not manufacture; our operations are not resource-intensive in the way those of 
industrial businesses are. Our material impact and our greatest opportunity lie in 
two areas: measuring and managing our own footprint with discipline and using 
our digital infrastructure to help more than 11 Lakhs merchants across more than 22 
countries transact with less paper, less travel and less waste.
Our environmental strategy follows this dual lens: reducing the footprint we own and scaling the low-
carbon commerce we enable. As a first-time reporter, we have prioritised building credible baselines and 
the governance needed to act on them, ensuring that ambition is matched by accountability.

WASTE MANAGEMENT
We manage waste responsibly, guided by prevention, segregation at source, 
resource recovery and regulatory compliance. Given our service-oriented business, 
waste is largely confined to offices and is non-hazardous. We segregate dry and wet 
waste at source, supported by housekeeping protocols and periodic reviews.
Why
itmatters
We deploy and retrieve 
payment hardware at 
scale across our merchant 
network, which makes the 
lifecycle of our devices, not 
our office bins, the materially 
important waste question 
for our business. Managing 
that lifecycle responsibly, 
alongside disciplined office 
waste and water practices, 
is both an environmental 
obligation and a matter of 
operational good sense.RESPONSIBLE E-WASTE MANAGEMENTReducing waste at source
	yDigitising business and employee-lifecycle processes to cut paper consumption
	yPromoting reusable alternatives and reusing packaging from supplies and

	yEmployee awareness on responsible disposal, plus segregation and recycling of 
plastic waste through authorised channels
Electronic waste from end-of-life IT assets is managed in line with 
applicable E-Waste (Management) Rules. Laptops, peripherals and other 
equipment are channelled through authorised recyclers and Producer 
Responsibility Organisations for sound dismantling and disposal, with 
relevant entities maintaining valid Extended Producer Responsibility 
authorisations and take-back mechanisms.

consumption and waste at source.

Global economy[1]
The global economy remained 
resilient in CY 2025 despite rising 
trade tensions and geopolitical 
uncertainty, growing by 3.4%. 
Advanced economies expanded 
by 1.9%, led by the United States 
(2.1%) and Europe (1.4%), while 
emerging and developing 
economies grew 4.4%, supported 
by China’s 5.0% growth and 
India’s 7.6% expansion, driven 
by strong domestic demand, 
resilient services and sustained 
public investment. Continued 
investments in AI, semiconductors 
and digital infrastructure 
further supported economic 
activity, although geopolitical 
developments and energy supply 
disruptions continued to create 
market volatility.
Global growth is projected to 
expand to 3.1% in CY 2026 before 
improving to 3.2% in CY 2027, 
while global inflation is expected 
to ease from 4.4% in CY 2026 to 
3.7% in CY 2027. Despite near-
term uncertainties, technology-
led investments are expected to 
remain a key growth driver. At the 
same time, rapid adoption of real-
time payment infrastructure and 
embedded finance is transforming 
global commerce by enabling 
faster settlements, integrated 
financial services and more 
seamless customer experiences.
[2]  With India expected to remain 
one of the fastest-growing major 
economies, these trends are 
creating a favourable environment 
for the continued expansion of 
digital payments and fintech 
infrastructure.

India's payment stack goes global
India's digital payment infrastructure is increasingly 
being adopted beyond its borders through UPI-enabled 
cross-border payment linkages. UPI is now operational 
across Singapore, UAE, France, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka,

India's payment stack.India: Leading the global real-time payments revolution6 
India has emerged as the world’s leading real-time 
payments market, driven by its Digital Public Infrastructure 
(DPI), widespread UPI adoption and strong regulatory 
support. The country’s interoperable payments ecosystem 
has transformed digital commerce, enabling instant, 
secure and low-cost bank-to-bank transactions at an 
unprecedented scale. Today, India accounts for nearly 49% 
of global real-time payment transaction volume, making it 
the world’s largest real-time payments ecosystem.

Company overview
Pine Labs is the commerce 
operating system for the Global 
South and a technology company 
focused on digitising commerce 
through digital payments and 
issuing solutions for merchants, 
consumer brands, enterprises and 
financial institutions. In practice, 
its platform enables a retailer 
to accept any form of payment, 
offer an on-the-spot EMI solution, 
issue a branded gift card and 
reconcile everything in one place. 
It enables a bank/fintech to launch 
a full credit card programme 
without building core processing 
infrastructure and deploy and 
manage payment, affordability, 
issuing and commerce solutions for 
its clients. It helps an enterprise run 
its channel incentives, employee 
rewards and consumer promotions 
from a single platform. The 
Company connects merchants, 
consumer brands, enterprises and 
financial institutions through a 
unified commerce platform. It helps 
businesses accept payments, issue 
prepaid and credit products, offer 
affordability solutions and manage 
customer engagement from a 
single platform. Pine Labs operates 
across 22+ markets spanning India, 
Southeast Asia, the Middle East, the 
US and Africa, delivering integrated 
commerce infrastructure rather 
than standalone products.
Today, over 11 Lakhs merchants, 
750+ consumer brands and enterprises and 200+ Financial 
institutions operate on its platform, 
processing approximately ₹17.2 
Lakhs Crores in gross transaction 
value and more than 2 Crores  
transactions every day.
The Company’s platform 
comprises four layers, including 
transaction infrastructure 
powering omnichannel payment 
acceptance; a value-added 
services layer running one of India's 
leading point-of-sale affordability 
marketplace; an issuing and 
acquiring platform enabling 
brands and banks to issue, accept, 
store and move value at scale; and 
a data intelligence layer converting 
transaction data into merchant 
insight and AI-native services. In 
FY 2025-26, this compounding 
model delivered Revenue from 
Operations of ₹2,711 Crores, 
Adjusted EBITDA of ₹559 Crores, 
PAT of ₹113 Crores and Operating 
Cash Flow of ₹395 Crores, a 
financial profile that reflects both 
the scale of its infrastructure and 
the improving margin mix as the 
Company move up the stack. The 
Company’s strategy is anchored 
across three dimensions: a multi-
product platform spanning the full 
commerce stack, a multi-segment 
reach from large enterprises to 
the growing mid market and a 
multi market footprint that exports 
India's battle-tested fintech 
infrastructure to emerging and 
developed markets alike.

Powering commerce at scaleServing industry leaders at scale in IndiaAgentic commerce[8]
Agentic commerce refers to a 
model in which Artificial Intelligence 
(AI) agents autonomously 
discover, evaluate and execute 
transactions on behalf of users, 
enabling a seamless and proactive 
commerce experience.  
Agentic commerce is emerging as 
a transformative trend in digital 
commerce, with the global B2C 
retail market expected to generate 
USD 3–5 Trillion in revenue through 
AI-driven commerce models by 
2030. Rapid advancements in AI 
capabilities and the ability of AI 
agents to operate on existing digital 
infrastructure are accelerating 
adoption. As AI systems become 
capable of managing increasingly 
complex transaction workflows, 
agentic commerce is expected 
to shift the ecosystem from user-
driven interactions to AI-mediated 
transactions, reshaping demand 
generation, decision-making and 
transaction execution across the 
commerce value chain.

The Company’s business model
The Company generates revenue from two platforms serving merchants, brands, enterprises and 
financial institutions-
The Company’s Digital Infrastructure and Transaction Platform spans three offerings-
(i)  In-store and online infrastructure — payment solutions covering multiple payment methods, software, 
billing integrations, settlements, automated reconciliation, merchant dashboards, on-site servicing and 
omnichannel capabilities including payment aggregation, tokenisation and payouts.
(ii)  Flow, Affordability and Transaction Processing — an affordability ecosystem linking merchants, brands 
and credit issuers at checkout with real-time approvals and fraud checks; an offers platform; trade-ins; and 
flow-based services such as dynamic currency conversion, UPI, wallets, pay by points, loyalty and payment 
aggregation services.₹400+ Cr
Revenue  
(FY 2025-26)

Overview of performance
FY 2025-26 marked a defining year 
in Pine Labs’ journey, demonstrating 
the strength of its platform-led 
growth model. Over the last three 
years, Pine Labs scaled platform 
GTV at a CAGR of 57%. During 
FY 2025-26, on average, Pine Labs 
processed more than 2 Crores 
transactions daily and expanded 
its DCP base to 20 Lakhs+ 
touchpoints, translating into 
sustained revenue growth while 
improving operating efficiency. 
Over the last three years, Pine Labs’ 
revenue expanded at a CAGR of 
19%, while international revenue 
grew at a CAGR of 44% during 
the same period. Pine Labs is witnessing a shift in its revenue mix 
from more distribution-led revenue 
to a higher mix from consumer, 
brand and payment value pools. 
The mix of revenue from consumer 
brands and payment value 
pools has increased from 58% in 
FY 2022-23 to 66% in FY 2025-26, 
along with an expansion in the 
revenue mix of business services 
and data value pools. 
A favourable shift in revenue 
mix, combined with operating 
leverage from higher business 
scale, supported a significant 
improvement in profitability, 
with Adjusted EBITDA margin 
increasing from 9% in 
FY 2023-24 to 21% in FY 2025-26.  Pine Labs reported a Profit After 
Tax of ₹113 Crores in FY 2025-26, 
reversing from of ₹145 Crores in 
FY 2024-25, while operating cash 
flow improved by 8x  to over ₹395 
Crores during the same period. 
These milestones reflect the 
successful conversion of scale into 
profitability and cash generation, 
creating a stronger foundation for 
long-term growth.

Performance

Direct expenses
Direct expenses in FY 2025-26 were 
₹669 Crores, an increase of ₹124 
Crores (23%) YoY from ₹545 Crores 
in FY 2024-25, with the majority 
of the increase driven by higher 
distribution costs:
	 Distribution cost for Prepaid 
Cards grew by ₹94 Crores 
(35%) YoY to ₹364 Crores in 
FY 2025-26 from ₹270 Crores 
in FY 2024-25. This reflects 
our deliberate investment in 
expanding our distribution 
prowess to deliver a holistic 
value proposition for brands 
in acquiring, retaining and 
growing their customers. We 
are approaching each market 
with a full-stack strategy: we 
acquire marquee processing 
brands in global markets, then 
expand into distribution to 
deepen relationships and build 
stickiness. This playbook has worked well in India, and we are 
now executing it globally.
	 Connectivity and operational 
costs reduced to ₹130 Crores 
in FY 2025-26 from ₹141 Crores 
in FY 2024-25, with disciplined 
cost optimisation which more 
than offset any increase from 
a growing POS base and our 
international scale-up. Beyond 
efficiency, we are enabling 
AI-driven capabilities on our 
devices and expanding use 
cases, creating the opportunity 
to earn incrementally from flow 
and transactions, not just from 
subscriptions. COGS of DCPs 
increased modestly to ₹176 
Crores from ₹136 Crores, in line 
with upfront sale volumes. 
Direct expenses as a percentage 
of revenue remained largely 
stable, with contribution margin 
of ~75%, reflecting the Company’s 
continued discipline on unit 
economics even as it scales.
Segment-wise, Digital 
Infrastructure and Transaction 
Platform (DITP) contribution 
margins remained strong at 
~83%, while Issuing and Acquiring 
Platform (IAP) contribution margins 
held at ~58%, driven by a mix 
shift  towards higher distribution.

Opportunities and threats
Platform-led expansion
The Company is transitioning from 
a product-led to an integrated 
platform-led model, as a full-stack 
commerce and fintech partner 
rather than a point-solution 
provider. This shift is expected 
to expand wallet share through 
multi-product bundling across 
merchants, brands and financial 
institutions, while unlocking 
cross-business synergies that 
strengthen the Company’s 
enterprise proposition.
International scale-up
Building on the Company’s India 
foundation, the Company is scaling 
globally through a multi-market 
engine anchored in Southeast Asia, 
with expansion into the US, and the 
UAE. The Company is prioritising 
high-growth corridors, airlines, 
SMBs in SEA and market entry in 
the US, by replicating the India 
playbook through a platform-
led go-to-market approach and 
strong local partnerships.
Distribution and merchant scale
The Company is expanding its 
merchant footprint beyond its 
established enterprise franchise 
into the growing mid-market and 
SMB segments. The scaling of 
Woohoo 2.0 and reseller networks under IAP business and self-
serve, affiliate and partner-led 
acquisition channels across in-
store and online payments is 
expected to support continued 
merchant and transaction growth.
Affordability expansion
The Company continues to 
expand its affordability ecosystem 
beyond consumer electronics into 
categories including furniture, 
fashion, healthcare, automobiles, 
wheels and other emerging 
consumption segments. Growth 
is expected to be supported by 
new brands, UPI-led affordability, 
an expanding store network 
and greater adoption. The 
Company also expects to 
expand its addressable market 
across the full customer journey, 
from pre-transaction demand 
creation through in-transaction 
affordability to post-transaction 
engagement and monetisation.
Embedding prepaid across use 
cases
The Company’s prepaid 
issuance franchise offers a long 
growth runway through deeper 
adoption of existing use cases, 
expansion into new brands and 
categories and international 
growth. New opportunities include 
gaming, employee benefits and 
international markets expansion, alongside the expansion of prepaid 
programmes across airlines and 
other emerging use cases.
Agentic commerce and AI-led 
payments
AI agents are enabling 
autonomous discovery, decision-
making and payments, creating 
an emerging opportunity for Pine 
Labs to power secure, agent-led 
commerce and payments across 
merchants and consumers.
Threats
While the industry continues 
to expand, certain structural 
challenges persist. Evolving 
regulatory requirements and 
coordination across a broad 
ecosystem of partners, including 
brands, financial institutions and 
merchants, require continued 
execution. The shift toward agentic 
workflows also introduces new 
questions around the identity 
and authentication of transacting 
agents, requiring the Company 
to evolve its platform and risk 
frameworks accordingly. At the 
same time, rising transaction 
volumes call for continued 
investment in cybersecurity and 
platform resilience, while the pace 
of technological change demands 
ongoing innovation.

Risk management
Risk Description Mitigation Strategy
Strategic 
riskIt is the risk to earnings and capital 
arising from a lack of responsiveness to 
changes in the business environment, 
adverse business decisions or the 
adoption of inappropriate strategies 
and choices.Management adopts a proactive approach 
to changes in the economic and business 
environment. Business strategies are 
regularly reviewed with senior officials of 
the organisation to enable timely strategic 
decision-making. Significant strategic 
matters are also referred to the Board, 
whose members bring diverse experience 
across their respective fields, for detailed 
deliberation and informed decision-making.
Operational 
risk Operational risk is defined as the risk 
of loss resulting from inadequate or 
failed internal processes, people or 
systems or from external events. It also 
includes fraud risk, information security 
and cybersecurity risk, technology risk, 
product risk, business resilience risk 
and legal risk.	 Review of operational loss incidents, 
along with detailed Root Cause Analysis 
(RCA), is undertaken by the concerned 
department and where required, by 
cross-functional teams to identify 
corrective and preventive actions. The 
Risk and Compliance team review the 
incident and RCA, following which the 
incident is reported to the ERMC. The 
corrective actions and implementation 
timelines are tracked by the ERMC. 
	 Fraud Risk management policy is in place 
and effectively implemented. 
	 The Company’s policies are documented 
and approved by the Board.
	 The Company strives to promote 
an appropriate risk culture in which 
employees are aware of operational 
risks and are encouraged to learn from 
their mistakes.
Compliance 
riskPine Labs India, as a fintech company, 
falls under the regulatory purview 
of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), 
NPCI, FIU, Card Networks, SEBI and 
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. In 
addition, the Company is required 
to comply with various central, state 
and commercial laws applicable to 
the conduct of its business activities. 
Any non-compliance with mandatory 
regulatory requirements may result 
in compliance risk and expose the 
Company to penalties imposed by 
regulatory or statutory authorities.The Company recognises that the regulatory 
landscape is subject to periodic change and 
therefore remains proactive in preparing 
for evolving regulatory requirements. 
The Company responds effectively to 
regulatory changes, maintains constructive 
relationships with regulators and authorities, 
strengthens its capital position and enhances 
the quality of its in-house compliance 
framework. All regulatory reports, returns 
and disclosures are submitted accurately 
and in a timely manner to reflect the correct 
position.

riskFinancial risk refers to any event

(B) Technology absorption-
(i) the efforts made towards technology absorption;
(ii) the benefits derived like product improvement, cost reduction, product development or import 
substitution;
 (i) Efforts Made Towards Technology Absorption
  During the year, the Company undertook a broad portfolio of strategic technology absorption initiatives 
focused on artificial intelligence-led automation, customer experience, operational excellence, 
engineering productivity, platform modernisation, reliability engineering, security intelligence and 
scalable payment infrastructure.
  Within the Credit+ platform, the Company deployed an agentic AI platform designed to automate and 
augment operational support functions. The platform has been integrated into day-to-day operations 
and autonomously handles a significant proportion of routine Level-1 support activities, including 
resolution of portal access issues, handling of technical and functional queries, report generation and 
ad-hoc file processing.
  The Company also initiated the implementation of Last9, an AI-enabled observability and Site Reliability 
Engineering platform, to strengthen application and infrastructure monitoring, intelligent incident 
detection, operational visibility and root cause analysis.
  The Company commenced a strategic cloud-native modernisation programme to transition the Credit+ 
platform from its legacy Oracle-based architecture to AWS Aurora PostgreSQL. The programme involves 
the adoption of cloud-native technologies, automated deployment and operational practices, scalable 
architecture patterns and enhanced resilience engineering.
  The Company also developed Jarvis, a Large Language Model-agnostic multi-agent framework with an 
integrated harness layer and a specialised prepaid knowledge base enabling launch of various Agentic 
Use Cases.
  AI-enabled customer interaction capabilities were expanded through customer-facing chatbots and 
production-grade email and conversational agents, including the Email AI Agents and PineOne Chat AI 
Agent. These solutions are intended to enable faster issue resolution, improve responsiveness, increase 
self-service adoption and reduce dependency on traditional customer support channels. 
  Predictive analytics capabilities were also implemented for early identification of risks, including merchant 
churn prediction.
  AI agents and automation solutions are being deployed across merchant onboarding, program 
activation, helpdesk operations, code development and review, testing and regression processes. Model 
Context Protocol, or MCP, servers have been developed to facilitate API-based self-service onboarding 
and enable clients and internal systems to securely interact with relevant platform capabilities. MCP-
based solutions are also being developed for the payment gateway platform and other programmable 
payment use cases.
  RAG models and tools have been implemented to retrieve and contextualise logs, telemetry and 
operational information for on-call teams, thereby supporting faster incident analysis and root cause 
identification.
  Autonomous operational capabilities have also been introduced through AI-driven self-healing systems 
for point-of-sale devices and applications. These solutions identify and resolve defined anomalies without 
manual intervention, supporting improved device availability, application performance and operational 
continuity.
  Technology absorption initiatives were extended across the security lifecycle to improve threat detection, 
risk analysis, control validation and remediation. These initiatives include AI-driven false-positive analysis, 
zero-day vulnerability advisory, automated information technology general controls validation, automated 
issue remediation and security scanning of software code during the pull-request process.
  The Company has also implemented an AI-driven scheme configuration and offer enablement solution 
to automate configuration workflows, validations, exception handling and deployment activities. 
  Enterprise-scale platforms have been developed to drive end-to-end business automation, including 
an AI Virtual Employee platform enabling multi-functional agentic execution with real-time system 
integrations (Agentic Org – AI Virtual Employee Platform)
  Collectively, these initiatives reflect the Company’s continued investment in artificial intelligence, automation, 
cloud modernisation, observability, reliability engineering and security to build a future-ready, scalable, 
resilient and efficient payments ecosystem.

 (ii) Benefits Derived
  The technology absorption initiatives undertaken during the year have resulted in measurable and 
expected benefits across customer experience, operational efficiency, engineering velocity, service 
reliability, system performance, security, scalability and cost optimisation.
  The deployment of AiVAR has enabled automation of approximately 80% of routine Level-1 support 
activities, resulting in an estimated 50% reduction in manual operational effort. This has contributed to 
faster response times, improved customer experience and greater scalability of support operations.
  The increased adoption of chatbots and AI-assisted customer interaction channels has enabled a larger 
proportion of customer queries to be resolved through self-service. This has reduced customer support 
contacts, improved response and resolution times and allowed support operations to scale without a 
corresponding increase in operating costs. The Email AI Agents have delivered an approximately 70% 
reduction in turnaround time, with the potential for up to 90% reduction in associated manual effort.
  The PineOne Chat AI Agent has been piloted across more than 200 merchants, with plans for wider 
deployment. Merchant churn prediction models have achieved approximately 80% prediction accuracy, 
supporting proactive intervention and better decision-making.
  AI-assisted development workflows, engineering agents and automated code reviews have delivered 
an estimated 25% improvement in developer productivity. Faster code review cycles and increased 
automation across development, testing and deployment have reduced engineering bottlenecks and 
enabled teams to focus on higher-value activities, thereby supporting faster delivery of new features and 
platform enhancements.
  RAG-powered incident intelligence solutions have reduced initial incident analysis and triage time from 
approximately 30 minutes to less than 5 minutes, representing an improvement of more than 80%. Faster 
access to relevant logs, telemetry and contextual data has supported quicker root cause identification 
and reduced Mean Time to Resolution for production incidents. 
  The implementation of Last9 is expected to further enhance platform availability through proactive 
monitoring, intelligent incident detection, AI-assisted root cause analysis and shorter incident resolution 
timelines.
  AI-driven merchant onboarding automation has increased automation coverage from approximately 
35% to 80% across relevant workflows. Approximately 30% of onboarding use cases are now fully zero-
touch, reducing manual intervention, improving process consistency and supporting higher onboarding 
volumes. 
  MCP-enabled self-service capabilities are expected to further simplify integration and onboarding for 
clients.
  Program activation turnaround time has been reduced from approximately four hours to less than two 
minutes through AI-enabled automation. This has improved adherence to service-level commitments, 
eliminated manual processing bottlenecks and enabled near real-time activation for customers.
  Quality engineering and test automation initiatives have significantly accelerated release cycles. 
Regression testing duration has been reduced from approximately six hours to five minutes, while feature 
testing execution time has decreased from approximately five days to two hours. Increased automation 
coverage has also improved testing consistency, defect detection and overall product quality.
  AI-enabled self-healing capabilities for point-of-sale devices and applications have autonomously 
resolved approximately 56% of identified anomalies and contributed to an improvement of more than 
50% in application and device performance. These capabilities have reduced manual intervention and 
strengthened service continuity and platform reliability.
  The security initiatives have enhanced accuracy, reduced operational noise and automated control 
validation and remediation. AI-based false-positive analysis has reduced noise by approximately 80% 
while achieving accuracy of more than 90%. ITGC automation has achieved 100% automated coverage 
with accuracy of at least 99%. Automated issue remediation has delivered an approximately 80% auto-fix 
rate and savings of nearly 300 person-hours per month, while automated pull-request security scanning 
has generated savings of more than 50 person-hours per month. Zero-day advisory capabilities have 
also enabled real-time evaluation of emerging security risks.
  The scheme automation solution has improved the speed, quality and scalability of offer enablement 
by reducing manual configuration effort, minimising validation errors and compressing implementation 
timelines from approximately one to two days to a few minutes.

  The cloud-native modernisation programme is expected to deliver long-term benefits through lower 
infrastructure and database licensing costs, improved system performance, enhanced scalability, 
greater operational agility and stronger platform resilience. It will also provide a modern foundation for 
product innovation and faster delivery of new capabilities.
  Collectively, these initiatives have strengthened the Company’s in-house technological capabilities, 
reduced dependency on manual processes and external systems, improved customer and employee 
experiences and enabled scalable, repeatable and efficient operations. They also support the 
Company’s long-term digital transformation strategy and its objective of building resilient, intelligent

from 06 June 2025. Pursuant to the Scheme, the

been transferred to and vested in the Transferee 
Company with effect from the 06 June 2025.

6.16 INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND 
(IEPF)
 Pursuant to Section 124 and 125 and other applicable 
provisions of the Act, read with the Investor Education 
and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, 
Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 (“IEPF Rules”), 
dividends which remain unpaid or unclaimed for a 
period of seven years from the date of transfer to 
the Unpaid Dividend Account shall be transferred 
by the Company to the Investor Education and 
Protection Fund (“IEPF”).
 The IEPF Rules mandate companies to transfer all 
shares in respect of which dividend has not been 
paid or claimed for seven consecutive years or more 
in the name of IEPF. The Members whose dividend/
shares are transferred to the IEPF Authority can 
claim their shares/dividend from the IEPF Authority 
following the procedure prescribed in the IEPF Rules.
 During the year under review, the Company was 
neither liable to transfer any amount to the Investor 
Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), nor was any 
amount lying in the Unpaid Dividend Account of the 
Company for the Financial Year 2025-26.

REPORT ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE 
GOVERNANCE:
Pine Labs Limited (“Pine Labs”) believes that good 
corporate governance is essential for achieving long-
term sustainable growth and creating value for all 
stakeholders. The Company is committed to conducting 
its business with integrity, transparency, fairness 
and accountability, while ensuring compliance with 
applicable laws, rules and regulations.
The Company’s governance framework is designed to 
promote ethical business conduct, effective decision-
making and responsible management. The Board of 
Directors provides strategic direction and oversight to 
ensure that the Company’s management acts in the 
best interests of its stakeholders, including shareholders, 
customers, employees, partners and the community.
Pine Labs strives to maintain high standards of disclosure, 
internal controls and risk management practices. The 
Company also fosters a culture of openness and ethical 
behaviour through well-established policies, including 
a Code of Conduct and vigil mechanism, enabling 
employees and other stakeholders to report concerns in 
a secure and transparent manner.
Through its corporate governance practices, Pine Labs 
aims to uphold the principles of integrity, accountability 
and responsible business conduct, thereby strengthening 
stakeholder confidence and ensuring sustainable 
business performance.
BOARD OF DIRECTORS:
The Board of Directors of Pine Labs Limited (“Board”) 
provides strategic direction and oversight to the 
management and plays a pivotal role in ensuring that 
the Company operates in accordance with the highest 
standards of corporate governance.
The Board is responsible for guiding the Company’s 
strategy, monitoring management performance, 
ensuring compliance with applicable laws and 
regulations, and safeguarding the interests of 
all stakeholders.
The Board is fully aware of its roles and responsibilities in 
fulfilling its fiduciary duties. The Board Members strive to 
meet the expectation of operational transparency while 
ensuring the confidentiality of information.
The composition of the Board is structured to ensure an 
appropriate balance of executive and non-executive 
directors, including independent directors, who bring 
diverse expertise, experience and is in conformity with 
Regulation 17(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing 
Regulations/SEBI (LODR)”) and the Companies Act, 
2013 (”Act”) comprising of 6 (Six) Directors including a 
Chairman and Managing Director, a Whole-time Director 
and 4 (four) Non-Executive Directors. Out of 4 (Four) Non-
Executive Directors, 3 (Three) are Independent Directors.
The Board functions through various committees 
constituted in accordance with the applicable provisions 
of the Companies Act, 2013 and other regulatory 
requirements. These committees assist the Board in 
discharging its responsibilities in areas such as audit 
and financial reporting, nomination and remuneration, 
risk management and stakeholder relations.
Through regular meetings and active engagement with 
the management, the Board ensures that the Company’s 
operations are aligned with its strategic objectives 
while maintaining robust governance standards and 
protecting the long-term interests of stakeholders.
None of the Director(s) on the Board:
	 holds directorships in more than ten 
public Companies;
	 serves as Director or as Independent Director in 
more than seven listed entities; and
	 The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 
does not serve as an Independent Director in 
any listed entity.

D. BOARD PROCEDURE AND FLOW OF INFORMATION:
	 The Board meets at least once a quarter to 
review the results and other items on the 
agenda and once a year for approval of 
annual budgets and strategy. When necessary, 
additional meetings are held.
	 The Board periodically reviews the business 
performance of the Company and its key 
subsidiaries and risk management matters.
	 The quarterly, half-yearly and annual results of 
the Company are first placed before the Audit 
Committee of the Company and thereafter the 
same are placed before the Board.
	 A Compliance Certificate, signed by the Chief 
Financial Officer and the Chairman, Managing 
Director and Chief Executive Officer to the 
Company is placed before the Board on a 
quarterly basis that the financial results do not 
contain any false or misleading statement or 
figures and do not omit any material fact which 
may make the statements or figures contained 
therein misleading.
	 The Board/Committee Meetings (“Meetings”) 
are convened by giving a detailed notice 
and agenda setting out the business to be 
transacted at the meeting(s).
	 The notice and agenda papers are circulated 
to the Board by the Company Secretary / 
Company Secretary team or the person 
authorized by the Board of the Company along with the explanatory notes and these are 
distributed in advance to the directors. Every 
member of the Board is free to suggest the 
inclusion of items on the agenda.
	 All divisions/departments in the Company 
are encouraged to plan their functions well in 
advance, particularly with regard to matters 
requiring discussion/ approval/ decision in the 
meetings. All such matters are communicated 
to the Company Secretary or the person 
authorised by the Board of the Company in 
advance so that the same could be included 
in the agenda for the meetings. The agenda 
papers are prepared by the concerned officials 
of the respective departments.
	 Minutes of the proceedings of the Meetings 
are prepared within the stipulated time as per 
applicable law and thereafter the same are 
circulated to all Directors for their comments. 
The minutes of all the Committees meetings 
and meetings of the Board of Directors 
of the Company are placed before the 
Board and the respective Committees.
	 The Board/Committee also passes resolutions 
by circulation on a need basis. The Company 
has been providing the directors with an 
option to participate in Meetings through 
electronic mode.
	 Minimum information as specified in Part A of 
Schedule II of SEBI (LODR) is periodically placed 
before the Board.

B  NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION COMMITTEE:
 The Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
(“NRC”) of the Company has been constituted in 
accordance with the Section 178(1) of the Act and 
Regulation 19 of SEBI Listing Regulations. The role of 
the NRC is to oversee the selection of directors and 
senior management personnel based on criteria 
related to the specific requirement of expertise and 
independence. The NRC evaluates the performance 
of directors and senior management personnel 
and recommends to the Board the remuneration 
payable to directors and senior management 
personnel of the Company. TERMS OF REFERENCE OF THE NOMINATION AND 
REMUNERATION COMMITTEE:
 The terms of reference of the NRC are as under:
 a)  to formulate the criteria for determining 
qualifications, positive attributes and 
independence of a director and recommend to 
the Board a policy relating to the remuneration 
(fixed pay, variable pay, and incentive), of the 
directors, key managerial personnel, and senior 
managerial personnel;
 b)  to formulate criteria for and a mechanism of 
evaluation of the performance of independent 
directors and the Board. For every appointment 
of an independent director, the Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee shall evaluate 
the balance of skills, knowledge and experience 
on the Board and, on the basis of such 
evaluation, prepare a description of the role 
and capabilities required of an independent 
director. The person recommended to the 
Board for appointment as an independent 
director shall have the capabilities identified in 
such description. For the purpose of identifying 
suitable candidates, the Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee may:

agency, if required;
  ii. Consider candidates from a wide range 
of backgrounds, having due regard 
to diversity; and
  iii. Consider the time commitments of 
the candidates:
 The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, while 
formulating the above policy, should ensure that:
 1. The level and composition of remuneration be

E.  RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE:
 The Company has constituted a Risk Management Committee (“RMC”) and adopted the Risk Management 
Policy duly approved by the Board of Directors. Currently, the Company’s Risk Management approach comprises 
of the following:
Annual Report 2025-26  |  117
Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements

=== page 121 ===
	 Identification of Risks
	 Assessment and Mitigation of Risks
	 Monitoring and reporting of Risks
 The Company follows a three line of defence 
model for management of risks, wherein the first 
line of defence (business and support units) owns 
and manages the risks, with the second line (risk 
management) supporting the first line in managing 
and mitigating the risks followed by the third 
line (internal audit). Organization wide risks are 
monitored and reported to the RMC at periodic 
intervals with the RMC regularly apprising the Board 
of the recommendations discussed in its meetings 
and actions taken by it.
 Brief description of terms of reference:
 The terms of reference of the RMC are as under:
 1. Formulate a detailed risk management policy 
which shall include:
  i.  A framework for identification of internal 
and external risks specifically faced 
by the listed entity, including financial, 
operational, sectoral, sustainability 
(particularly, ESG related risks), 
information, cyber security risks or any 
other risk as may be determined by the 
Risk Management Committee.
  ii.  Measures for risk mitigation including 
systems and processes for internal control 
of identified risks.
  iii.  Business continuity plan.
 2. Review and approve policies of the Company 
involving all material risks including but not 
limited to information security risk, vendor risk, 
compliance risk (including compliance policy, 
KYC and AML policy and FPC), and other risks.
 3. Implement and monitor policies and/or 
processes for ensuring cyber security.
 4. Ensure that appropriate methodology, 
processes and systems are in place to monitor 
and evaluate risks associated with the business 
of the Company.
 5. Monitor and oversee implementation of 
the risk management policy, including 
evaluating the adequacy of risk management 
systems and plans. 6. Periodically review the risk management policy 
and systems at least annually considering 
the changing industry dynamics and evolving 
complexity and further recommendation to the 
Board for approval.
 7. Keep the board of directors informed about 
the nature and content of its discussions, 
recommendations and actions to be taken.
 8. Appointment, removal and terms of 
remuneration of the Chief Risk & Compliance 
Officer shall be subject to review by the Risk 
Management Committee. The Chief Risk and 
Compliance officer shall report to RMC directly 
on quarterly basis on overall direction to the 
risk management.
 9. Approve the risk appetite statement and KRIs, 
for the Company.
 10. Review on annual basis appropriateness and 
effectiveness of risk governance.
 11. Oversee fraud risk.
 12. Coordinate its activities with other committees, 
in instances where there is any overlap 
with activities of such committees, as 
per the framework.
 13. Any other similar or other functions as may be 
laid down by Board from time to time and/or as 
may be required under applicable law.
 The Risk Management Committee shall have 
powers to seek information from any employee, 
obtain outside legal or other professional advice 
and secure attendance of outsiders with relevant 
expertise, if it considers necessary.
 Two meetings of the Risk Management Committee 
were held during the year. The equity shares of the 
Company were listed on BSE and NSE on November 
14, 2025 and the Company entered the list of top 
1000 listed entities based on market capitalization 
as of December 31, 2025. In accordance with the SEBI 
Listing Regulations, the Company is provided with a 
period of three months from the date of applicability 
to comply with the relevant provisions. Accordingly, 
the requirement to hold RMC meetings became 
applicable from April 1, 2026. However, as part of 
good corporate governance practices and since 
the Company already had a Risk Management 
Committee, the RMC meetings were conducted on 
January 27, 2026 and March 27, 2026 respectively at 
which proper quorum was present.

F. Information Security Committee
 The Company has also constituted an Information 
Security Committee (ISC) in accordance with the 
requirements of applicable provisions of the Reserve 
Bank of India Master Directions on Cyber Resilience 
and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank 
Payment System Operators dated July 30, 2024.
 Brief description of terms of reference:
 The terms of reference of the ISC are as under:
 1. Primary oversight over information security 
risks, including cyber risk and cyber resilience 
for the company.
 2. Review and monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) 
to identify potential risk events and Key 
Performance Indicators (KPIs) to assess the 
effectiveness of security controls.
 3. IT assessment reports (such as system audit, 
VA / PT reports, etc.) shall be placed before the 
Committee in the meeting due immediately 
after such report is available.
 4. Review the recurring observations for the 
deficiencies reported in the security testing of all the application along with detailed analysis 
for recurrence and resolution.
 5. Review on an annual basis the independent 
information and cyber security audits of 
Cloud Service providers (CSP) along with 
the CSP’s overall performance and its cyber 
resilience capabilities.

In compliance with the Act and SEBI Listing Regulations, 
the Company provided members the facility to vote 
electronically (‘remote e-voting’) for the postal ballot and 
also appointed Ms. Ritu Mahajan (ACS No.: 35495 CP No.: 
22918) of M/s. Ritu Mahajan and Associates, Practicing 
Company Secretary, as the Scrutinizer to scrutinize the 
postal ballot and remote e-voting process in a fair and 
transparent manner. All e-votes received up to 5.00 
p.m. on February 13, 2026 were considered for scrutiny. 
E-votes received after this date were not considered for 
scrutiny. The results of the Postal Ballot were announced 
on February 17, 2026 declaring that the special resolutions 
set out in the Postal Ballot Notice were duly passed by the 
Members of the Company, with requisite majority.
Procedure adopted for Postal Ballot:
1. Postal ballot notices, including voting instructions, 
were sent via email to members who had registered 
their email IDs with the Company or depositories, 
pursuant to the MCA’s General Circular nos. 
14/2020 dated April 08, 2020, 17/2020 dated April 
13, 2020, 20/2020 dated May 05, 2020, read with 
other relevant circulars issued in this regard, the 
latest being General Circular No. 03/2025 dated 
September 22, 2025 permitting electronic voting. 
Additionally, provisions were made to enable other 
members to register their email IDs to receive the 
postal ballot notice and cast their votes online. 
The said notice of postal ballot is also hosted on 
the website of the Company at the following link: 
https://cdn.pinelabs.com/india/investors/pdf/
legal-documents/PBN-SE-PLL.pdf2. The advertisement was published in the Newspapers 
viz. ‘Financial Express’ (English) and ‘Jansatta’ 
(Hindi) on Wednesday, January 14, 2026 giving the 
requisite details as per the provisions of the Act and 
Secretarial Standard - 2.
3. The remote e-voting period began on Thursday, 
January 15, 2026, at 9:00 a.m (IST) and ended on 
Friday, February 13, 2026, at 05:00 p.m. (IST).
4. The Scrutiniser submitted her Report on Monday, 
February 16, 2026 and the resolutions were deemed 
to have been passed on the last date of remote 
e-voting i.e., on Friday, February 13, 2026.
Further, there is no special resolution proposed to be 
conducted through postal ballot.

COMMUNICATION TO INVESTORS:
INVESTOR GRIEVANCES REDRESSAL THROUGH THE SEBI 
COMPLAINTS REDRESS SYSTEM (SCORES) PLATFORM:
SEBI vide its circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 
dated 20 September 2023 stated that a complaint lodged 
in SCORES platform will automatically be forwarded to 
the concerned entity with a copy to designated body.
Entity will upload Action Taken Report (ATR) on SCORES 
within 21 days from the receipt of the Complaint. Failure 
which, the designated body will take cognizance of the 
complaint for first review of the resolution through SCORES 
and ask Company to submit ATR to the designated body. 
The complainant may seek a second review by SEBI of 
the Complaint within 15 calendar days from the date of 
the submission of the ATR by the Designated Body.
SEBI vide its press release PR No.06/2024 dated 01 April 
2024, launched the new version of the SEBI Complaint 
Redress System (SCORES 2.0). The new version of 
SCORES strengthens the investor complaint redress 
mechanism in the securities market by making the 
process more efficient through auto-routing, auto-
escalation, monitoring by the ‘Designated Bodies’ and 
reduction of timelines.
Investors can lodge complaints only through new version 
of SCORES i.e. https://scores.sebi.gov.in from 01 April 
2024. In the old SCORES i.e. https://scores.gov.in investors 
would not be able to lodge any new complaint. However, 
investors can check the status of their complaints 
already lodged in old SCORES and pending in the old SCORES. Further, the disposed off complaints filed in the 
old SCORES can be viewed at SCORES 2.0.
ONLINE RESOLUTION OF DISPUTES (ODR):
SEBI has introduced a common Online Dispute Resolution 
Portal (‘ODRP’) which harnesses online conciliation and 
online arbitration. 
In case a member is not satisfied with the resolution 
provided by the company/RTA, then the online dispute 
resolution process can be initiated through the ODR 
portal at https://smartodr.in/login.

14. PROCESS AND MANNER FOR E-VOTING:
 i) In compliance with the provisions of Section 108 
and other applicable provisions of the Act, read 
with Rule 20 of the Companies (Management 
and Administration) Rules, 2014 as amended, 
and Regulation 44 of the SEBI Listing Regulations 
and in terms of Section VI-C of SEBI Master 
Circular dated January 30, 2026 in relation 
to the e-Voting facility provided by listed 
entities, the Company is providing the facility 
of remote e-Voting to its Members in respect 
of the business to be transacted at the AGM. 
The Company has engaged the services of KFin 
for facilitating e-Voting to enable the Members 
to cast their votes electronically as well as for 
e-Voting during the AGM. Resolution(s) passed 
by Members through e-Voting is/are deemed 
to have been passed as if it/they have been 
passed at the AGM. 
 ii) Members are provided with the facility for 
voting through an electronic voting system 
during the VC/OAVM proceedings at the AGM 
and Members participating at the AGM, who 
have not already cast their vote by remote 
e-Voting, are eligible to exercise their right to 
vote at the AGM.
 iii) Members who have already cast their vote by 
remote e-voting prior to the AGM, will also be 
eligible to participate at the AGM but shall not 
be entitled to cast their vote again on such 
resolution(s) for which the Member has already 
cast the vote through remote e-voting.
 iv) Members of the Company holding shares as on 
the cut-off date i.e. Wednesday, September 9, 
2026, may cast their vote by remote e-Voting. 
The remote e-Voting period commences on 
Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 09.00 a.m. 
(IST) and ends on Tuesday, September 15, 
2026 at 05.00 p.m. (IST). The remote e-Voting 
module shall be disabled by KFin for voting 
thereafter. Once the vote on a resolution is 
cast by the Member, the Member shall not be 
allowed to change it subsequently. The voting 
right of Members shall be in proportion to their 
share in the paid-up equity share capital of 
the Company as on the cut-off date, being 
Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
